clue.text: Son studying about pressure and expansion?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the son-and-studying string wraps round the pressure symbol

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
P is the physics symbol for pressure
reading a subject at university means studying it

explanation.surface: A student son whose academic work is growing in some unspecified way.
explanation.walkthrough: S and READING sit either side of P, giving SPREADING; the question mark flags the definition as a loose noun use.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading, used as a noun, is the act of extending outwards, which is a kind of growth over a wider area.

clue.text: Young Italian men in irons GI set free

indicators.note: things set free are released from their fixed order, so these letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Young Italians held in shackles are released by an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Signorino is the Italian form of address for a young gentleman; signorini is its plural.

clue.text: Regret drinking ordinary and ultimately rotten port

indicators.note: a word that drinks something takes it inside itself
ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: to rue something is to regret it
O is a common abbreviation for ordinary
the final letter of rotten

explanation.surface: Someone regrets drinking a commonplace port wine that has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine being drunk, but here it is a harbour city: O goes inside RUE, then N follows to give ROUEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is a major French city on the Seine with a large inland river harbour.

clue.text: Mixologist's alpine tip for cocktail?

indicators.note: a mixologist mixes drinks, so these letters are mixed up too

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A bartender passes on a mountain-themed recommendation for a mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An appletini is an apple-flavoured martini, a popular mixed drink served in a cocktail glass.

clue.text: Island gallery in which Queen perform again

indicators.note: in which says the following item sits inside the gallery just named

blocks.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island
the Tate is the famous London art gallery
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: The rock band Queen play a repeat gig at an island art venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the rock band, but it is the monarch's royal cipher, as on a postbox.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do something over again, repeating a process or action.

clue.text: Corporation that's hosting extremely hyper singer

indicators.note: a host holds guests inside, so that's surrounds the next piece
extremely points to the two end letters of the following word

blocks.note: corporation is old jocular slang for a pot belly
i.e. is short for id est, that is
the outer letters of hyper

explanation.surface: A company playing host to a very excitable vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a business, but it is old slang for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Guthrie was the American folk musician who wrote This Land Is Your Land; his son Arlo also sings.

clue.text: Hidden store of money an auditor notices

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so what is noticed is a sound rather than a spelling

blocks.note: money in coins and notes is cash, which is pronounced the same as the target word

explanation.surface: An accountant spots a secret stash of funds during an audit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant checking the books; here it simply means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a concealed hoard of supplies, valuables or weapons kept for later use.

clue.text: Holiday destination beset by manic April

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the wanted word is enclosed within the following letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A vacation spot overrun by crowds during a frantic spring month.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples, a famously glamorous resort for tourists.

clue.text: Italian painter travelling on cattle around area

indicators.note: things travelling are on the move, so these letters shift position
around means the jumbled letters wrap themselves about the next piece

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An artist from Italy journeys about the countryside riding livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the eighteenth-century Venetian artist celebrated for his views of Venice and London.

clue.text: Stop polishing off Coke and Southern Comforts

indicators.note: polishing off means finishing or getting rid of, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: to cease is to stop
C is short for cocaine, of which coke is slang
S is the standard abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Someone told to quit drinking cola and Southern Comfort whiskey liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coke' and 'Southern Comfort' read as drinks; C is dropped from CEASE and S added, giving EASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Comforts as a verb means relieves or soothes, the same as lessening pain or worry.

clue.text: Awfully prim guest is surly in the extreme

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so these letters come out in a mess

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A dreadfully prudish visitor proves extremely bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of grumpy, meaning most bad-tempered, matches surly taken to its furthest degree.

clue.text: Quiet piece of music without intro soprano hums

indicators.note: without its intro means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a song is a piece of music
S is the standard abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A soft tune with no opening bars, which a soprano hums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hums' looks like singing, but it is the British slang sense of smells bad.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang both words mean gives off a nasty smell, so stinks is the shared sense.

clue.text: Big cat of little weight

blocks.note: first meaning: the snow leopard of Central Asian mountains
second meaning: a small imperial unit of mass

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a paradox, a large animal that is light; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the snow leopard and also a unit of about twenty-eight grams, a sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Those possibly pumped to take a shot?

definitions.text: Those possibly pumped to take a shot?

blocks.clueFragment: Those possibly pumped to take a shot?
blocks.note: surface reading: people psyched up before having a go at something, or before a drink
setter's reading: guns charged with compressed gas by a pump action before firing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pumped' suggests excited people about to attempt something; literally it describes guns primed by pumping.
explanation.definitionFit: These are guns firing pellets by compressed gas, often charged by pumping a lever before each shot.

clue.text: Where one finds detectives screening Old Bill

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind, so the detectives' word wraps round the next item

blocks.note: where something is found is in a place
the vice squad is the police unit dealing with gambling and prostitution
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Police detectives protecting a veteran officer from scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police, which fits the detective story; Bill alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill sent to a customer listing goods or services and the payment due.

clue.text: Six heading to Burma and helping in quake

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
the first letter of Burma
a ration is a portion or helping of food

explanation.surface: Six aid workers travel to Burma to help after an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor or shaking movement of the ground is a vibration, so quake works as a noun here.

clue.text: Conservative dons left in high spirits

blocks.note: people who left a room exited it
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Tory university lecturers from the political left are in a jolly mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like Oxbridge lecturers and 'left' like politics; really C goes inside EXITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrilled or worked up with eager enthusiasm is to be lively and buoyant in mood.

clue.text: I dance not wildly, showing self-control

indicators.note: done wildly means done without order, so these letters scatter

blocks.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone restrained enough to refuse to dance with abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who keeps emotions in check is restrained or composed, which is held in.

clue.text: Minister splits parties over drug control

blocks.note: a do is a party; the plural asks for two different ones
Min is the standard abbreviation for minister
the ANC, the African National Congress, is a political party
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A government minister drives a wedge between parties over drugs policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'parties' asks for two different ones: a social gathering and a South African political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance means having power or authority over others, the same as being in command.

clue.text: To sum up, one with new pants will get end away

indicators.note: getting the end away removes the final letter of the word before

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the standard abbreviation for new
briefs are a style of underpants

explanation.surface: A crude boast that a man in fresh underwear is going to get lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get one's end away' is British slang for having sex, which drives the cheeky surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means briefly or in summary, used when giving a short account.

clue.text: Belligerent Dutch striker

blocks.note: someone belligerent is in favour of fighting, or for war
D is the standard abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: An aggressive attacking footballer from the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description of a player, but splits as FOR WAR plus D.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a striker plays at the front of the team as an attacker, the role of a forward.

clue.text: Do what's expected of prisoner with record

blocks.note: con is short for convict
in British slang form is a criminal record

explanation.surface: What society demands of an ex-convict with previous convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to follow accepted rules and behave as others require.

clue.text: Funny, but firm physician

blocks.note: Co is short for company
a medic is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor who is amusing yet strict with patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective for the doctor; it is a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedic means relating to comedy and so humorous or amusing.

clue.text: One beaten in spades by underarm bowling

indicators.note: bowling sends things rolling about, so these letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: S is the card-game abbreviation for spades
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed comprehensively by a bowler using a lowly underarm delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In spades' suggests thoroughly; underarm bowling is a gentle delivery style in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument struck with sticks, so it is something beaten.

clue.text: Cops finally arrest one hiding in home?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before

blocks.note: the last letter of cops
to nail a criminal is to catch or arrest them

explanation.surface: Police at last detain a fugitive hiding in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the home is a shell carried on the creature's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail withdraws into its shell for protection, so it hides inside the house it carries.

clue.text: Holy festival not ultimately pious, one scoffs

the last letter of pious

explanation.surface: A religious festival with an irreverent attendee who mocks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffs' looks like mocking, but it is the British sense of eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is British slang for wolfing food down, so someone who scoffs is an eater.

clue.text: A writer hugging small tree

indicators.note: something hugging another wraps its arms around it

blocks.note: taken as written
a pen is something you write with
S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An author embracing a little sapling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author; it is a pen, which hugs S.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar with leaves that tremble in the slightest breeze.

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before

blocks.note: the last letter of Trump

clue.text: Ace record from celebrity

blocks.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
a list is a written record of items

clue.text: After relinquishing power, bear old PM

blocks.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power
Paddington is the marmalade-loving bear of children's books

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like a verb meaning endure; it is the famous fictional bear, minus P.

clue.text: I must get hands around inveterate singleton

explanation.definitionFit: A loner habitually avoids company and prefers to be by themself, a person always solitary.

clue.text: Debauchery in 80s perhaps pleasant, I expressed

nice means pleasant
taken as written: this is the letter removed
